dataset_family: Single-centre retrospective memory-clinic cohort: Center for Cognitive Disorders and Dementias, Geriatrics Unit, S. Orsola-Malpighi Hospital, Bologna, Italy (143 consecutive MCI outpatients, April 2015 to January 2019)
method_family: Clinical-cohort prognosis of one-year MCI-to-AD conversion. Univariate converter vs non-converter comparison (Mann-Whitney), backward-elimination logistic regression with bootstrap, ROC and a dichotomised scoring system. Brain CT (MTA, Fazekas) and FDG-PET read visually and with SPM.
what_it_shows: Muscari et al. 2021, Arch Gerontol Geriatr 94:104359. The PDF title, authors and DOI 10.1016/j.archger.2021.104359 match the block and the map. In 143 MCI outpatients, baseline GDS-15 did not differ between the 31 patients who converted to AD within one year and the 112 who did not: Table 1 gives NO 1 [0.5-3] vs YES 1 [0-3], p = 0.63. Only variables with p < 0.05 went into the logistic models, so GDS never entered either model. The authors conclude that depressive symptoms were not predictive of conversion. GDS < 5 was an inclusion criterion and psychiatric disorders an exclusion criterion, so every patient sits in a sub-clinical 0-4 band (Table 1 labels the row 'GDS (0-5)'). GDS is never related to the CT or FDG-PET measures.
why: PARTLY. The paper shows only the conversion part of the Table A1 severity sub-clause: a baseline continuous severity score did not track conversion. This is the same kind of result as P-647, with four limits. (1) RANGE RESTRICTION. Entry required GDS < 5, and psychiatric disorders were excluded, so severity was tested only inside a 0-4 band. The null is partly built in, and it says nothing about MCI with clinically relevant depressive symptoms. This comes close to, but is not the same as, the exclusion artefact round 20 found in P-662: here GDS IS tested against an outcome. (2) UNIVARIATE ONLY. The test is a Mann-Whitney comparison in Table 1. The Table 4 footnote lists the variables entered into the models, and GDS is not among them. (3) SHORT HORIZON. Follow-up is one year, with 31 converters. (4) BRAIN MEASURES UNTESTED. GDS is never related to CT MTA or FDG-PET. All participants have MCI, so the first clause (depression status associated with MCI) cannot be tested either. INDEPENDENCE. The dataset (Bologna S. Orsola-Malpighi) is distinct from P-643 (Korea University Guro), P-647 (Shanghai Brain Health Cohort), P-662 (Shanghai Tongji) and P-663 (Florence), and from the other candidates (HABS-HD, ADNI-3, LBC1936). No author is shared; the Muscari/Lunardelli Bologna group is not the Naples group of P-770. The method family, clinical-cohort conversion prognosis, is the same broad family as P-647 (cohort survival plus ROC). It would add a new dataset family but arguably not a new method family. GLYPHS. The '<' in 'GDS <5' survives in the extract and is corroborated by the Table 1 row label 'GDS (0-5)', so no decoding was needed. Not a preprint.

quotes.quote: This retrospective study included 143 MCI outpatients (76.6±5.2 years, 46.8% women). Baseline variables were common neuropsychological tests (including Mini Mental State Examination-MMSE and Montreal Cognitive Assessment-MoCA), brain CT and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-PET. Outcome variable was CAD after 1 year.
The patients admitted to the study had the following inclusion criteria: - Age ≥60 years - MMSE ≥24 - GDS <5
Exclusion criteria were: previous stroke, alcohol or drug abuse history, epilepsy or psychiatric disorders, or possible organic causes for the cognitive deficit.

Among neuropsychological tests, MMSE, MoCA and CDT provided significantly lower scores in converters than in nonconverters. Instead GDS score, which can also be affected by age, education and comorbidities, did not differ between the two groups.
(Table 1) AD conversion NO YES P value (N=112) (N=31) [...] GDS (0-5) 1 [0.5-3] 1 [0-3] 0.63

To establish which associations between the above parameters and AD conversion were independent, the variables associated with P values <0.05 in Tables 1 and 3 were included in two models of logistic regression, with backward elimination procedure of the nonsignificant associations (Table 4).

(Table 4 footnote) Model A: female, education, MMSE, MMSE-recall, MoCA, MoCA-executive, MoCA-denomination, right MTA, left MTA. Model B: like model A, plus FDG-PET predictivity of AD and FDG-PET right temporal, left temporal, right cingulate gyrus, left cingulate gyrus, left precuneus hypometabolism.
In addition, in agreement with previous studies, we found that depressive symptoms are not predictive of conversion
